input.quote: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: § 7.2 imposes an MFN on us, not on Vendor: we would have to extend Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms we give any other technology supplier. It is open-ended — no defined product or service, no time limit, and no reasonable-comparison carve-outs — so it fails the fallback (MFN limited to a defined product, 12 months, with comparison carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory. It also directly contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. Preferred position is no Customer-side MFN, so we delete § 7.2; any MFN granted by Vendor in our favour is unaffected.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted the open-ended obligation for us to give Vendor our best terms offered to any other supplier, as our playbook does not accept MFN obligations running against the customer; this also conflicts with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. Vendor-granted MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.
